content: The test image shows a microscope view of stem tissue with numerous small black dots scattered across pale/tan fibrous tissue. This pattern suggests fungal structures (pycnidia or microsclerotia) on stem tissue. Key candidates: Charcoal_Rot (microsclerotia), Diaporthe, Phomopsis.

Based on my analysis, the test image is a microscope view of stem tissue with **numerous tiny black dots** scattered across pale/cream-colored fibrous tissue. This is the classic microscopic appearance of **Charcoal Rot** (*Macrophomina phaseolina*), where microsclerotia (tiny black structures) are embedded throughout the stem/root tissue — giving it the "charcoal dust" appearance under magnification. The name "charcoal rot" literally derives from this powdery black microsclerotia pattern on the tissue.

Key evidence:
- Microscope view of stem longitudinal section
- Abundant small, uniform black dots (microsclerotia) scattered throughout
- Pale/fibrous tan-white background tissue
- No pycnidia ring patterns (ruling out Diaporthe/Phomopsis)
- No larger structures (ruling out White Mold sclerotia)
